**Status:** accepted numerical Result mechanics outside the new report surface
remain `STABILIZED`. `ReportPanel`, automatic report selection, and the pure
report composer are a `CONVERGING` candidate. Structured authoring, its
identity integration, and certified diagrams are another `CONVERGING` scope
with an integrated implementation baseline; see the
[central evidence status](../contracts/index.qmd#implementation-evidence-status). Adaptive
presentation-theme semantics remain a separate `CONVERGING` candidate.

## Separate materialized values from analysis evidence

`Result` is the shared immutable, already-materialized value role.
`AnalysisResult` is the receipt-backed terminal subset and exposes immutable
`ResultIdentity(plan_sha256, request_sha256, attempt_sha256, result_sha256)`.
`DirectSolveResult`, `DiagonalRootResult`, `OptimizationResult`, and
`HBBatchResult` derive from it. Each HB batch contains one `HBCaseOutcome` for
every declared case. The outcome is a derived view of its parent receipt: a
success exposes matrices and states; a numerical failure exposes its stored
`HBCaseFailure`. `ExplanationResult`, `CircuitDiagramResult`, and
`ReportResult` remain derived values and do not fabricate operation receipts.

## Reconstruct typed Results in Python

Python verifies the receipt and manifest before constructing an
`AnalysisResult`. Scalars and axes become SCNSim-registry Pint Quantities;
matrix payloads become labeled NumPy arrays with ordered coordinate, mode,
frequency, unit, and load-state metadata. An Analysis Result retains request,
attempt, artifact, and runtime identity even when its chunks load lazily.

Direct matrix channels use `(coordinate, ())`. HB input and output channels use
flattened `(coordinate, mode)` pairs in coordinate-major/mode-minor order.
`MatrixView.input_channels` and `output_channels` expose those exact stored-axis
labels; presentation never infers a reshape or relabels a mode.

HB operating-point arrays use the separate structured axes
`(pump_mode, node_coordinate)`. Each pump-mode label is an ordered integer tuple
in request pump-axis order, and each node-coordinate label is the sealed
compiler identity recorded by `state_node_map`. These labels are evidence, not
new View selectors or Port aliases.

The Result catalog describes artifact meaning: role, dtype, shape, axes, units,
and channel order. HB links carry case-local `{case_id, id, path, sha256}`
references. The manifest instead seals the byte tree. A repeated local ID or
SHA-256 across cases is valid; only the complete receipt-bound reference has an
addressable role.

No Result unpickles arbitrary Python objects. Missing chunks, mismatched shape,
unit disagreement, forbidden non-finite values, or a real/imag manifest
mismatch fails verification instead of returning a partial typed object.

## Keep presentation downstream of execution

Plotly renders every numerical Result surface. `plot()` returns one detached
native `plotly.graph_objects.Figure` without displaying it; `show()` displays
the same presentation exactly once and returns `None`, preventing a final
notebook expression from displaying its MIME representation a second time.
Editing a Figure returned by `plot()` cannot mutate verified Result arrays,
evidence, or identity. `add_to(fig, row=..., col=..., ...)` adds one
explicitly selected trace, heatmap, or table to a compatible caller-owned
subplot and returns the same Figure. It never replaces the caller's template,
layout, or unrelated traces. Every inserted native trace carries its complete
x/y physical semantics, display units, and source Result/View/point identity.
An occupied subplot must have compatible axis semantics before any mutation;
frequency coordinates are converted to its established compatible display
unit, while parameter refs and categorical channel bases must match exactly.

Matrix response plots select channels from the stored
`MatrixView.input_channels` and `output_channels`. An omitted channel pair uses
the first stored pair and labels it visibly; a coordinate string must resolve
uniquely, while `(coordinate, mode)` selects one exact channel. The default
response contains magnitude and wrapped phase; an explicit component creates a
single-component figure. Exact-frequency table and heatmap views use the whole
stored channel-ordered matrix and never interpolate. Tables retain real and
imaginary values with units. Heatmaps require one real-valued component.
Incompatible or unused arguments fail instead of being ignored.

S magnitude accepts `magnitude="linear" | "db"`; dB is
$20\log_{10}|S|$. Exact zero remains negative infinity and has undefined
phase. A dB response whose complete finite span is under 0.1 dB starts with a
0.1 dB viewport so numerical roundoff is not magnified into a visual feature;
the exact values and hover data are unchanged, and callers may zoom or update
the detached Figure. Dimensionful Y/Z families remain linear because no reference-unit API
exists. Scalar quantities use evidence tables, not invented curves. Sweep,
operator, HB, and completed Optimization presentations use the same trace,
heatmap, and table builders; missing and failed values remain explicit gaps or
status rows rather than zeros. A partial scalar Parameter field pairs its gaps
with visible source-index, parameter-identity, and typed-failure evidence; an
all-failed field is a status table rather than an empty curve or exception.

`OptimizationResult.plot()` shows completed total-cost history plus the exact
winner summary. `kind="objective"` or `kind="residual"` requires one explicit
`objective=` ID, `kind="parameter"` requires one `parameter=ParameterRef`, and
`kind="table"` shows each candidate status/cost, retained objective value,
normalized residual, weighted cost, component status, and every term value,
View lineage, status, and failure. These are views of the completed ledger,
never live optimizer progress.

Numerical presentation lazily imports Plotly only when `plot()`, `show()`,
`add_to()`, or report assembly is requested. Solve, evaluate, optimize, and
resolve do not import Plotly or Kaleido. Native Plotly HTML export is supported
without a browser or network dependency. Static Plotly export is optional and
requires separately installed Kaleido/Chrome support; SCNSim adds no export
wrapper and never opens a browser or downloads an engine automatically.

```bash
uv sync --extra static-export
```

This installs Kaleido; a compatible Chrome/Chromium installation remains an
explicit host prerequisite for `Figure.write_image(...)`.

Every numerical theme entry accepts only `Theme.AUTO`, `Theme.LIGHT`, or
`Theme.DARK` and raises `TypeError` for raw strings. `AUTO` resolves at Figure
construction to Plotly's configured default template; detached Figures do not
track later OS/browser media changes. `LIGHT` and `DARK` are deterministic.
Report assembly resolves `AUTO` once from that same configured Plotly template
and applies its paper background, text, grid, and first accent colors to the
report body and tables; it does not add browser/OS theme tracking. A custom
template with an omitted body color uses Plotly's ordinary light fallback.
The independent SVG diagram surface retains its existing adaptive `AUTO`
semantics, Schemdraw `Drawing`, and Matplotlib-backed helpers.

Notebook diagram display continues to wrap the same SVG in self-contained
zoom, pan, copy, reset, and open controls. If JavaScript or clipboard access is
blocked, ordinary scrolling and the static SVG remain readable. These controls
do not alter the returned object, its geometry, a report, or static output.

The light and dark palettes share one paired ten-color cycle. Changing theme
cannot change arrays, curve/case order, line count, labels, diagram geometry,
layout, topology, or Plan/request/Result identity.

| Role | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| background | `#ffffff` | `#111827` |
| foreground | `#243044` | `#eaf2fb` |
| secondary text | `#5b677a` | `#a8b7ca` |
| grid/border | `#d8e1ec` | `#2b3a4f` |
| primary accent | `#2f80d1` | `#7bb7f0` |

The paired line cycle, in order, is
`#2f80d1/#7bb7f0`, `#c76b00/#f2a65a`, `#2e7d32/#7dcc8a`,
`#7e57c2/#b39ddb`, `#c44536/#ff8a80`, `#0f766e/#2dd4bf`,
`#a16207/#facc15`, `#be185d/#f472b6`, `#0e7490/#22d3ee`, and
`#475569/#cbd5e1`. Each pair is the light/dark rendering of one trace index.

## Structured diagram implementation target

The [diagram contract](../contracts/automatic-semantic-circuit-diagram-layout.qmd)
is the sole `CONVERGING` diagram authority. It consumes explicit series,
parallel, branch, bus, tap, link, exposure, coupling, and recursive ownership
facts from the independent
[assembly contract](../contracts/circuit-plan-assembly.qmd), not an inferred
neighbor partition or pre-render catalog.

The implementation baseline is integrated. The design below retains the
contract's required mechanisms; scoped validation does not establish universal
layout support, whole-course execution, or Human acceptance.

### Package and capture boundaries

Implementation remains separated behind private diagram boundaries:

| Boundary | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| snapshot and expected evidence | capture one immutable structured Plan; derive visible expectations and separate complete source rows |
| authoring IR | retain recursive scopes and explicit structured operators without intent inference |
| composition inventory and recipe | bind existing Blocks and owner-local attachments to one Plan; capture complete public settings and wiring |
| scene and local layout | measure native parts and child scenes, jointly place Blocks/anchors/junctions, and emit one neutral scene |
| layout constraints | verify requested shapes and sides against actual visible geometry separately from A/B |
| independent witnesses | reconstruct only visible electrical and ownership observations from the scene |
| frozen serialization | expose the checked scene through one immutable result |

Capture must be pure. Coordinate promotion and normalization operate on copied
records; the renderer cannot mutate a Plan temporarily and restore it. The
same capture feeds compiler preflight. The existing canonical encoder remains
the current implementation baseline. Target identity integration must
deliberately add the structural declarations rather than claiming compatibility
by similarity.

The expected-visible manifests derive independently from the structured source
snapshot or compiled expansion. Complete authored operator, exposure,
alias, parameter-definition, parameter-binding, effective-point, unit, bus,
tap, ground-provenance, and ownership records remain separate verified source
rows. Observed witnesses derive only from emitted neutral geometry and may not
read placement tables, source rows, or hidden answers.

### One public composition recipe

`SchematicComposition(plan=plan)`, `automatic(plan=plan, hints=None)`, and
`layout=None` share one fixed Default completion path. Explicit per-field
choices win; omitted axes, eligible orders, sides, and other fields receive
stable defaults. The constructor is partial-default, not a strict whole-manual
mode. Inspection is nonmutating. Hidden Composite contents remain
nonaddressable.

Blocks and attachment inventory retain the
[public composition contract](../contracts/automatic-semantic-circuit-diagram-layout.qmd#schematic-composition).
`replace_wiring(at=...)` still replaces one complete owner-local group:
incomplete edited attachments or arms fail at capture; Default never fills
missing manual wires. Bus/Link/public-Pin aliases in the same local class share
one authority, and old
wiring refs are invalidated. Subsystem Pins select parent-facing incidence;
ComponentInstance Pins select their occurrence-owner incidence. There is no
child-private fallback. `endpoint(pin)` resolves in that group; an ambiguous
Tap requires an explicit structure boundary. Ground networks and private Series
midpoints/Parallel rails cannot be generally replaced.

Local signal classes follow authored Bus/Tap, Link, exposure/backing, and
structural-boundary relations without crossing a child or physical body.
Equivalent public child pins may therefore join distinct parent-local groups;
their shared global net is carried by real child wiring, not a parent shortcut.
Only actual outward incidence supplies parent attachments. Open public pins
keep their boundary/side targets without imaginary wires, and a Port belongs
only to its root Bus's local class. Child measurement remains complete and
parent placement translates it whole. A/B and composition checks reconstruct
electrical continuity, named boundaries, and each local visible wire component
independently; sibling-group ink is not coverage for the selected group.

The existing axis/order/terminal/Port/tap/ground setters and
straight/L/T/Cross/connect primitives remain. Scope order contains independent
complete peers and child regions; Parallel order contains its complete
branches. Structures remain axis/endpoint Blocks, not extra scope peers.
`port_orientation()` atomically sets perpendicular boundary/load sides in the
root frame; `port_side()` preserves an explicit compatible load and rejects
incompatibility atomically. `ground_side()` does not accept Port. The complete
Port Block's external anchor is its circuit-facing lead end.

One captured AuthoringSnapshot, effective ResolvedPlanPoint, and display/font
settings feed one isolated Default completion, one measured body per child,
one constructive placement, and one fixed routing realization. Caller state,
refs, and old results never mutate. Authoring `diagram.composition` is the
detached immutable completed public recipe; compiled diagrams expose `None`.
Exact-Plan `to_composition(plan=plan)` returns a new editable fixed recipe.
Another single parameter point remeasures/reroutes without freezing pixels or
exposing editable private inventory. There is no reset-to-auto operation or
new request/schema/digest system.

Parallel-generated branch `SeriesRef` axis constraints, including those from
`SchematicLayout.axes`, are redundant constraints on the containing Parallel's
shared orientation, not independent Block rotations. Capture accepts equality
with the effective Parallel axis and rejects conflicts with branch/Parallel
IDs; setter order never chooses an override.

### Compiled matrix-stamp projection

The compiled projection remains a complete **matrix-stamp** view, never a
scalar-equivalent circuit. With the existing `exp(-i omega t)` convention and
$s=-i\omega$, each series station contributes

$$
Y_{\mathrm{series}} =
B_s (R + sL)^{-1} B_s^{\mathsf T},
$$

and each terminal half-shunt contributes

$$
Y_{\mathrm{half\text{-}shunt}} =
B_t (G/2 + sC/2) B_t^{\mathsf T}.
$$

The expansion evidence rows already contain half-scaled shunt coefficients;
the renderer must not divide them again. Both half-shunt contributions remain
visible and auditable. Symmetric entries describe one reciprocal coefficient
relation, not duplicate physical couplings.

Native diagonal glyphs associate a matrix coefficient with its station and
conductor. They are not independent executable scalar branches. Off-diagonal
$R$ is not a galvanic resistor, and off-diagonal $L$ remains a signed,
oriented mutual term. The visible table/legend retains every coefficient,
sign, unit, incidence, section/end/station, conductor order, and exact zero.
The observed witness reconstructs these facts from the neutral scene instead
of copying the expected table.

### Structured native scene and local layout

Authoring IR mirrors the declared hierarchy and operators. It does not derive
S/P/M interfaces, a quotient topology, a global physical flow, or a second
electrical graph. Every inline Subsystem and reusable Composite expands its
native child diagram in a measured ownership region with a visible ID.

### Resolve fixed defaults before measurement

Resolve sides and attachment identities once. Series default horizontal;
Parallel defaults vertical with start above end and branches left-to-right.
Peers follow declaration order along the scope axis without forced top
alignment. Explicit settings conjoin and never get overwritten. Parallel
branch axes follow their containing Parallel; the existing ground-side control
may determine a grounded structure's orientation.

Port boundary side comes from the selected wiring arm or intrinsic incident
direction, then the scope's leading side when undetermined (left for
horizontal, top for vertical). Horizontal Port loads default downward;
vertical loads default rightward. Explicit poses are never reselected around
obstacles. Public-boundary direction resolves from an explicit setting or
parent arm before child measurement. Attachment inventory follows
first-incidence insertion order: authored structures in declaration order
(external start/at boundary before end), then exposed scope pins, child public
pins, and independent complete-component pins; root Ports follow declaration
order. Real contact keys are deduplicated. `.tap()` declarations supply
membership and explicit-order validation, not a separate placement order.
Applicable explicit `tap_order` supplies a presentation precedence overlay
used by otherwise-Default arm assignment and constructive contact placement.
The immutable source inventory keeps its original order, and manual or fixed
wiring is not rewritten.
Unspecified ordering uses the structural/attachment declaration fallback,
while all explicit geometric constraints remain conjoined and validated.

Default uses the same public primitive builders as explicit wiring. Two
contacts use straight/L; three use a T with exact compatible directions or the
fixed scope branch (bottom for horizontal, right for vertical). Four distinct
directions use Cross, otherwise connected Ts. Larger groups use a fixed T
chain along the scope axis. Assign exact compatible arms first, then remaining
contacts/arms in stable source/cardinal order. No alternate trees, poses,
axes, or costs are enumerated. The five-map `SchematicLayout` convenience
feeds these same field setters and fixed completion.

### Construct one measured scene

Compact child measurement allocates only actually needed fixed route lanes on
each side, plus measured component and public-analysis labels, title, ground,
border, and escape space. Public-analysis labels are the exact named root Buses
and child Coordinates explicitly published by `expose_coordinate()`; anonymous
root Buses, private child Buses, anonymous internal IDs, and other exposure
kinds are excluded. Co-located public aliases share one measured multi-line
text run with every exact name on its own line, while the producer never merges
different owner-local source groups by `final_net`. These labels and their
nonconductive leaders are measured before
the final child frame, anchors, and fixed route lanes are committed.
Unused full-ring reservation and redundant straight-connector spacing are
removed. Frame and public anchors finalize together before parent translation;
there is no post-hoc crop, global clearance reduction, search, public coordinate
knob, or example-specific path.

Each child owns one measured native payload: upright labels, complete frame,
public anchors, local grounds, and reserved exits. Parent placement translates
that payload whole. Composite local/inverse-frame conventions remain intact;
neither its private contents nor measured anchors are rewritten. A single-pin
readout can hang from its parent T without inventing another Pin, Port, or
load. Complete native CPW/MTL bodies and scopes without child Subsystems follow
the same construction.

Preallocate measured Block, junction-subtree, Port/load/text, connector, and
coupling-guide strips. Branch extents can offset rows and enlarge subsequent
columns while preserving projected peer order; this is not top-aligned boxes
followed by late detours. A stable spanning traversal places each body once.
It is a placement device, not a wiring restriction: remaining edges and cycles
are each retained once in reserved closure tracks.

Allocate channels and distinct lanes in stable group/connection order before
emitting wires. Aligned routes are direct; prescribed bends and
channel/perimeter routes are arithmetic constructions. There is no reachable
authoring visibility graph, Dijkstra, candidate-position enumeration,
beam/backtracking, routing-order retry, or readability score, including inside
structural wiring, public-boundary/label completion, and mutual guides.
Reducing the previous search to a one-candidate limit is not this algorithm.

Native measurement, segment geometry, contact splitting, junction/jump
emission, final collision checks, and independent A/B/composition checks remain
shared building blocks. Different-net crossings use the existing jump
convention. Separate same-net routes cannot introduce incidental bridges,
add/erase requested T/Cross arms, or lose loop edges. Mutual guides occupy
nonconductive channels without acquiring placement or electrical authority;
coupling capacitors remain real authored conductive Blocks.

Unsupported fixed geometry fails with the actual scope, Block, junction, or
constraint. There is no fallback search, partial success, per-example renderer,
role/name guessing, or second authoring engine. Failure does not make the
electrical circuit invalid and is not proof of geometric impossibility.
Invalid input, stale/foreign/private/ground refs, and integrity errors retain
their fail-fast boundaries. Freeze the completed recipe with the same verified
scene; final source facts do not become observed A/B ink.

The compiled renderer and its routing remain unchanged. Authoring may reuse
shared segment/checking helpers but not compiled search functions. This
replacement defines no numerical timing threshold, timeout, public performance
control, scientific Gate, or universal two-dimensional embedding promise.

Local ground occurrences come from authored structural terminations, not a
scope-wide ground tree. A Parallel's shared grounded rail has one glyph;
independent grounded shunts each have their own, including both floating-network
shunts. Grounds default outward. `ground_side(...)` moves the grounded
termination's presentation side, rotating its structure if necessary without
changing electrical orientation or domain. Parent-applied pins and Port loads
retain their separate graphical roles while all glyphs denote the same
canonical reference.

The current renderer revision retains the local `U = 2.2` setting, actual font
metrics, separate readable name/value boxes, registered anchors, obstacle
clearance, continuous same-net paths, true T junctions, and other-net jump
arcs. `U = 2.2` is an implementation setting, not a TARGET semantic threshold
or user Gate. The main authoring image uses conventional native symbols, wires,
junctions, Ports, local grounds, physical coupling marks, and subtle titled
ownership regions. Operator/debug marks, routing guides, and private aliases do
not appear in that image. Ownership regions and labels remain unmistakably
nonconductive. Literal authored local IDs remain literal display identities;
the renderer neither title-cases them nor invents compact aliases. The existing
`show_provenance=True` default emits a compact separated footer that can be
hidden without changing the circuit scene or evidence. Public analysis names
remain visible when parameter values or provenance are hidden; neither switch
controls name publication.

An authoring `NodeMark` may be unlabelled; required compiled-marker labels stay
visible. A connected two-ray bend or contact may harmlessly carry a filled dot,
and every true three-or-more-ray wire junction carries one. Isolated dots and
marks that imply a different-net connection are invalid, but the renderer does
not reject a dot merely because it has only two incident rays. Mutual winding
dots are separate marks whose orientation evidence remains visible.

Ordinary L/JJ glyphs in the normal schematic need neither direction arrows nor
`+`/`−` reference-polarity signs. Ordered model endpoints and branch reference
conventions remain intact through rotation without being claimed as visible
facts of an unmarked symmetric body. Mutual winding dots, their endpoint
incidence, and coupling information retain sufficient visible relative polarity.
A presentation of signed branch current, voltage, or phase must explain its
reference endpoints. This is a presentation responsibility, not a new
signed-result API or a claim that diagram rendering computes those quantities.

Layout is deterministic only for the same renderer revision, inputs, Theme,
font files, and metrics environment. The contract does not prescribe a global
graph-search algorithm or promise all graphs are layoutable. Failure reports
the affected declaration or constraints and returns no partial/best-effort
certified result.

### Independent witnesses and frozen output

Composition-constraint verification checks requested shapes and sides against
actual emitted geometry, separately from A/B. Two connected Ts can preserve
electrical incidence yet violate an explicit Cross request. The neutral scene
contains neither expected composition nor ownership answer maps; witnesses
cannot use recipe metadata as if it were observed ink.

Unambiguous attachment rays can support layout checks. An ambiguous
multi-incidence Tap cannot support an independent exact Tap-name-to-picture
claim; its authored identity stays verified source evidence rather than an
observed scene fact.

Witness A reconstructs electrical bodies, terminals, wires, zero-wire
equivalence, grounds, Ports, couplings, and compiled matrix associations. It
checks authoring geometry against the exact Plan and point, or compiled geometry
against the exact compiler-emitted expansion for that Plan and point. This is
projection correspondence. In authoring projections with
`show_parameter_values=True`, A also
reconstructs every displayed effective scalar physical value and displayed unit
and compares them exactly in the deterministic six-significant-digit display
projection of that same resolved point. This is not a tolerance or bit-exact
Float64 roundtrip claim. The audit distinguishes displayed values from exact
source values. Hidden value labels make no
visible-scalar-label claim, although the certificate still binds the exact
effective point. This qualification does not weaken the compiled projection's
matrix, coefficient, sign, unit, half-shunt, or omission evidence.

Authoring scalar formatting uses Decimal `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` to six significant
digits with trailing zeros removed. It starts from the exact captured Float64
via `Decimal.from_float` and uses decimal SI scaling. The observed-value parser
does not round again: extra incorrect visible digits cannot be hidden by the
comparison. Dimensionful quantities use supported
engineering SI prefixes and `1 <= abs(mantissa) < 1000`, carrying to the next
prefix after rounding when needed. Zero is explicit and negatives retain their
sign; dimensionless values have no prefix. Outside the supported prefix range,
scientific notation preserves a nonzero value. Physical values, length, Port
reference impedance, and coupling coefficient use this display path without
altering exact model/source/parameter/request values or compiled formatting.

The N=1 CPW authoring Box retains kind/local ID, effective length when values
are enabled, and captured occurrence `n_sections` in both value modes, written
as `1 section` or `<N> sections`. It omits
conductor/reference/head-tail labels. A compares its two visible endpoints
without claiming ordered head/tail identity; exact identity and RLGC are
source-verified. MTL retains necessary ordered conductor/terminal evidence,
and compiled scientific evidence stays unchanged.

Open-pin observations come from actual visible stubs and terminal incidence,
never open flags, expected maps, or placement answers. A required cut connection
still rejects. All/partial open inline, built, nested, and rotated boundaries
use the same ink-bound evidence rule.

Source capture independently verifies each public Pin-to-Bus/Tap binding.
Witness B consumes only visible containment, contour crossings, and wire-contact
sets; it does not derive a hidden `bound => connected` requirement from source
metadata. A straight free-ending exterior root-Bus stub with no authored
external physical body or Port remains ordinary visible conductor rather than
an open child-boundary observation. A missing authored physical, Port, or real
boundary incidence still rejects instead of being excused as a free stub.

For unmarked ordinary symmetric two-terminal bodies, including L/JJ, A may
compare electrical evidence modulo endpoint-reference reversal. It does not
reconstruct an ordered endpoint pair from hidden placement, source rows, or
expected metadata, and missing polarity signs are not an audit failure.
Complete ordered model orientation remains separately verified source/provenance
evidence. For mutually coupled branches, A reconstructs relative polarity from
actual visible winding dots, their endpoint incidence, and coupling information;
a consistent reference reversal carries the corresponding coupling-sign
transformation, never deletion of sign evidence. Required oriented compiled
evidence remains unchanged.

With `show_parameter_values=True`, the mutual annotation exposes its signed
numerical coefficient. With values hidden, sign-only coupling information
(negative, positive, or zero) remains alongside visible dot/incidence evidence;
the hidden magnitude remains source-verified. A observes the sign in both modes
and the magnitude only when shown.

The witness is not an independent proof of numerical compiler lowering,
stamping, View/PTC realization, or solver correctness.

Witness B reconstructs visible child regions and headers, containment,
native-leaf and Port ownership, and cross-boundary electrical incidence. The
undrawn root envelope is scene bounds, not an observed ownership region. For a
single unlabelled child-boundary crossing, B checks visible wire incidence and
does not recover a hidden `PinRef` identity. It does not reconstruct invisible
operator IDs, link-call history, bus/tap names, or coordinate/branch/exposure
names. Internally, each B boundary record contains the visible region path,
parent, and literal local title; either an unlabelled-only boundary mode or its
visible named boundary; the electrical net; and the visible inside/outside
contact sets. It never stores a hidden exposure ID as an observed fact. Complete
aliases, parameter definitions and bindings, effective point, units, ground
provenance, and other authoring facts remain separately available as verified
source/provenance rows rather than being smuggled into scene metadata.
Public analysis-label correspondence is another independent visible
text-and-leader record: it verifies exact captured names and owner scope plus
the conductive-root net at the leader endpoint without using label text as
connectivity. Source aliases remain distinct lines in co-located text, and the
producer retains distinct owner-local groups when their source records share
one `final_net`. The observation does not independently distinguish swapped
labels at different contacts in the same scope on that same net; complete
owner-local grouping remains captured source evidence.
`audit.show()` labels observed A, observed B, visible-value checks, and captured
source/provenance as distinct evidence classes. Human review C alone decides
whether the Plan is the intended circuit.

Only after A/B agree is the neutral scene frozen. `CircuitDiagramResult.show()`
returns a real Schemdraw `Drawing` through a supported read-only facade. The
existing `Drawing.save()` remains the static API; there is no new save/export
method. Notebook controls and static fallback serialize the same scene.

The optional `presentation_sha256` excludes its own displayed annotation. It
is presentation identity, not an authenticity/security signature, and does
not alter Plan, compiler, request, Result, connectivity, semantic, or
expanded-graph identities.

### Engineer course alignment

The eight current QMD Chapter aggregates and generated zero-output Notebooks
teach the model-first workflow. Each Chapter is a complete clean-kernel
document; Lessons may share preceding state only inside that Chapter. Chapter
8 instead specifies two independent kernels over one preserved workspace.
They are documentation artifacts, not runtime evidence:

- Chapters 1–2 build the coupled grounded LC, inspect its Plan projection, and
  teach Direct/root Results, selected points, sweeps, and Optimization.
- Chapters 3–4 build the scalar feedline/readout and complete four-Port
  capstone before PTC and optional transform, quantity, and pump-off HB work.
- Chapters 5–6 teach deliberate Composite publication/reuse and bounded
  diagram customization on unchanged Plans.
- Chapter 7 teaches ordered N=2 RLGC, labeled four-Port channels, and separate
  authoring/compiled diagram limitations.
- Chapter 8 persists Results and a Report, then reconstructs and resolves the
  exact root request in a second independent kernel.

Every ASCDLS diagram remains a projection of the explicit authored or compiled
Plan. It may bind one explicit `ParameterSet`, including an optimization
winner supplied by the caller; it rejects `ParameterSpace`. It does not create,
select, or depict a request-specific View, PTC-effective topology, or solver
Result. Exact point/audit identity belongs to the
[Parameter System Contract](../contracts/parameter-system.qmd#parameterized-diagrams).

Selected Engineer-course diagram exports are source-bound evidence, not a claim that
all course cells executed. The central evidence status retains current
limitations; Human acceptance and durable stabilization of reopened semantics
remain separate lifecycle steps.

## Assemble reports from explicit inputs

`ReportSpec.inputs` contains exact `AnalysisResult` objects already held by the
caller, and `ReportSpec.theme` selects the same strict presentation enum used
by diagrams and figures. `ReportPanel` binds one of those exact objects by
object membership and normalizes once to a closed response, matrix, summary,
outcomes, or history selection. Selector groups are mutually exclusive and
unused fields are rejected. The same object may not occur twice in `inputs`;
distinct independently verified objects remain distinct even when their
canonical identities match. Supplying response selectors while omitting
`kind` is an explicit response, not an automatic panel whose selectors can be
discarded.

Response channels normalize to exact `(coordinate, mode)` members of the
selected Result. Matrix frequencies must be exact materialized points, and
Optimization objective and parameter histories must name members retained in
the completed ledger; a parameter selector must match the retained full
definition, not only its definitions/parameter IDs. A failed HB case has no
matrix payload: a response panel may select only its case or an exact
trace/channel pair captured from the verified request, and the report displays
that requested selection as unavailable alongside the typed failure, including
both declared endpoint coordinates and modes for a named trace.

The `CircuitRun.build_report()` facade retains Run ownership validation, then
passes only verified Results and normalized selections into the pure report
composer. The composer has no Run, workspace, process, or execution callback.
It preserves each native grid and records every failed HB or sweep outcome.
Its HTML and embedded native Plotly Figures use one theme; `AUTO` resolves when
each Figure is constructed while explicit themes remain fixed.
It does not search
the workspace, infer a latest Result, run an analysis, interpolate curves, or
decide whether a Design Target passed.

Automatic presentation is a closed per-family choice. A 1x1 Direct matrix
adds S magnitude only; multichannel Direct and Operator Results add inventory
tables; scalar Evaluation adds its typed values; HB and Sweep add outcome
tables; Optimization adds cost history and winner/outcome evidence. Sweep
outcomes use only the public point metadata accessor and never access
`ParameterPointOutcome.result` or `collect()`. Explicit panels replace the
automatic figures for their source Result, not the report-wide identity table.
All numeric plots come from the same Plotly presentation helpers used by
standalone `plot()`/`add_to()`; report assembly is not a second plotting engine.

`ReportResult` is pure derived data, not a terminal operation. Its `save(path)`
accepts a new `.html` file beneath an existing parent, refuses overwrite,
writes atomically, and returns `Path`. The file is standalone and self-contained:
it embeds figures, summary tables, and complete source identities, but excludes
complete large raw arrays, workspace links, timestamps, and inferred PASS/FAIL.
Additional formats wait for a named consumer.

The report presentation digest covers source Result identities, normalized
panel records, input order, and theme. It is deliberately separate from every
calculation identity and does not assert authenticity. A report never stores
or returns executable Run capability.

Suffix, missing-parent, and existing-target checks use `ValueError`,
`FileNotFoundError`, and `FileExistsError`; other filesystem failures retain
their ordinary `OSError` subtype. Export creates no operation receipt.
